raw_response:
I've farmed these 8 mu for 40 years now. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and I pay attention when the agro-store owner explains things, but mostly I do what worked last year with small adjustments.

My land is split. I keep about 6 mu on the wheat-maize rotation — that's the main business, the grain feeds us and the rest goes to the buyer. The other 2 mu I put in cotton. Cotton used to be bigger around here but the price isn't what it was, still I keep a bit because the soil on that plot is lighter and cotton handles it better, and my wife does the picking.

**Winter wheat (6 mu):** I plant in mid-October after the maize comes off. I use the improved variety everyone here plants — 济麦 type seed from the village dealer, about 15 kg per mu. Before planting I spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu as base, plus about 20 kg of diammonium phosphate. At green-up in spring I topdress with 15 kg urea per mu — that gives me roughly 22 kg N, 10 kg P, 8 kg K per mu all told. I irrigate from the well twice — once before winter to lock in moisture, once at jointing. Spray maybe 2 times for aphids and powdery mildew. I expect around 500 kg per mu. If I skimp on nitrogen the grain is thin, and thin grain means the buyer pays less — not worth saving 30 yuan.

**Summer maize (6 mu):** Right after wheat harvest I sow maize directly, no-till with the seeder — saves time and the stubble holds moisture. Hybrid seed, 郑单 or 登海 type, about 2.5 kg per mu. I sideband 40 kg of compound (15-15-15) at sowing and topdress 20 kg urea at the big trumpet stage. So about 18 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. One irrigation at tasseling if the rain doesn't come. Two sprays — one for armyworm, one for borer. I expect 550 kg per mu. Maize here yields well if you don't run short of water at tasseling.

**Cotton (2 mu):** I plough this plot in spring — cotton needs loose soil for the roots. Improved variety, not the GM seed my neighbor uses; I stick with what I know. Before planting I put 40 kg compound plus 15 kg urea spread later, and some potash because cotton likes potassium — about 18 kg N, 7 kg P, 10 kg K per mu. Irrigate 3 times through the season. Cotton needs more spraying than grain — at least 5 applications for bollworm, aphids, mites. I expect about 260 kg seed cotton per mu. It's more work per mu than grain, but the 2 mu is manageable with family labor.

I'm not going to change much from last year. Fertilizer prices are a bit high this spring but I won't cut back — a thin crop costs me more than the fertilizer saves.
